minutes.headline: Assessors agreed to add 17E to the senior exemption warrant article; the only vote taken was to adjourn.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the principal assessor's status report (new HERO Act motor vehicle exemption for veterans, FY25 new growth, a new hire, a zoning inconsistency, and excise billing responsibility). Most of the meeting was spent on the draft Article 12 for the November town meeting covering senior exemption and deferral options. A town clerk letter showed the deferral interest rate was already reduced years ago, so the board dropped pressing the separate 41A article. Minutes review was postponed, and the meeting adjourned.

votes.outcome: passed (motion and second heard; all in favor, no count)

budget_items.what_was_said: A budget committee member asked about a split tax rate. The chair explained it does not change the total tax levy, only how the burden is distributed.

budget_items.topic: HERO Act motor vehicle excise exemption
budget_items.what_was_said: Veterans with total disability get a full motor vehicle excise abatement for one vehicle; the state reimburses the town in full, based on last year's amount.

The board signed an invoice from Vision for interim adjustments.
An invoice for the assistant's business cards was signed.
The limits adopted at the 2006 town meeting remain in force for the coming year.
Most applicants qualified; two married couples would not under the 2006 limits but will not have it taken away for the prior year.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors agreed to ask that 17E be added to the draft Article 12 senior exemption article, alongside 17F and 41D; Sarah is to redraft it.
After a town clerk letter showed the deferral interest rate was already lowered at an earlier town meeting, the board dropped a separate 41A article.
The board kept the 2006 income and asset limits for the 41C exemption in force for the coming year.
The board postponed review of the September 4 and August 19 minutes and the executive session minutes; the only vote taken was to adjourn.
The principal assessor reported a new HERO Act motor vehicle excise exemption for disabled veterans, which the state reimburses to the town.

why_it_matters: Article 12 is a draft for the November town meeting, so residents may be asked to vote on the senior exemption and deferral options, which change who pays less property tax and how the town's cash timing is affected.

Assessors reported that the state reimburses the town for the new veterans' motor vehicle excise exemption, so that cost does not fall on the tax levy, though the reimbursement is based on last year's amount.
